questionText: At the rate of 10% p.a. S.I., what sum of money will amount to Rs.4500 in a 5 year period?
hints: Interest for 5 years at 10% a year is 50% of the principal. So the amount is 150% of the principal.
Amount = Principal + SI. SI for 5 years at 10% = 5 × 10% = 50% of P.

questionText: What will be the simple interest on Rs.3000 at 12% p.a. for 5 years?
hints: Use SI = P × R × T ÷ 100. 1% of 3000 is Rs.30.

questionText: In how many years will Rs.2000 amount to Rs.3500 at simple interest of 5% p.a.?
hints: Amount − Principal = interest. Find how much interest comes each year (5% of 2000), then divide.

questionText: The rate of interest a bank offers for deposit is 6% p.a. S.I. What interest will Rs.8000 earn if deposited for 2 years?
hints: Use SI = P × R × T ÷ 100. 1% of 8000 is 80.

questionText: In how many years will Rs.4000 double at the rate of 12.5% S.I.?
hints: 'Double' means the interest earned equals the principal (Rs.4000). How much interest does Rs.4000 earn in one year at 12.5%?
T = SI × 100 ÷ (P × R). Here SI = P.

questionText: What sum of money will yield an interest of Rs.189 in 3 years at 9% p.a. simple interest?
hints: Use P = SI × 100 ÷ (R × T). First work out R × T = 9 × 3.

questionText: If Rs.3200 amounts to Rs.3680 in 3 years, then what is the rate of interest?
hints: Amount − Principal = interest. Then use R = SI × 100 ÷ (P × T).

questionText: In what time will Rs.25 become Rs.37 at 16% p.a. simple interest?
hints: Find the interest needed (37 − 25). Then find how much interest Rs.25 earns in one year at 16%.

questionText: Kedar borrowed Rs.12000 from his friend at simple interest. He returned his friend Rs.15600 in full settlement of his loan after 5 years. What was the rate of interest charged by his friend?
hints: Rs.15600 is the amount (principal + interest). Subtract to find the interest. Then R = SI × 100 ÷ (P × T).

questionText: Aniket borrowed Rs.18000 to open a grocery shop. He cleared off the loan by paying Rs.25,560 at the end of 3 years. Find the rate of interest.
hints: Rs.25,560 is the amount (principal + interest). Subtract to get the interest, then R = SI × 100 ÷ (P × T).

questionText: The simple interest earned on a certain principal at 8% p.a. in 5 years is Rs.160. What is the principal amount?
hints: R × T = 8 × 5 = 40, so the interest is 40% of the principal. If 40% = 160, what is 100%?

questionText: If Rs.26500 is deposited in a bank at 8% p.a. simple interest, what will be the amount at the end of 4 years?
hints: Find the interest first (P × R × T ÷ 100). The AMOUNT is the principal plus the interest.
Amount = P + SI.

questionText: If Rs.6420 amounts to Rs.10,272 in 4 years at SI, then what is the rate of interest per annum?
hints: Amount − Principal = interest. Then R = SI × 100 ÷ (P × T).

stepByStep.text: Interest = Amount − Principal: 10272 − 6420 = 3852, so the simple interest is Rs.3852.
So the rate is 15% per annum. 15% is not one of the choices given, so the answer is "none of these".

questionText: What principal amount will earn an interest of Rs.2205 in 12 months at 18% p.a. SI?
hints: 12 months = 1 year. So 18% of the principal is Rs.2205. Find 1% first.

questionText: In how much time will Rs.450 become four times of itself at 24% p.a. SI?
hints: If the money becomes 4 times, the interest earned is 3 times the principal (4 − 1). Find the interest per year at 24%.
T = SI ÷ interest per year.

questionText: Medha borrowed Rs.3500 from a friend at simple interest. After 3 years she repaid the loan by giving Rs.4340. What was the rate of interest per annum?
hints: The amount repaid includes the borrowed money plus interest. Subtract to find the interest, then use SI = P × R × T ÷ 100 to find R.
SI = Amount − Principal. R = SI × 100 ÷ (P × T).

questionText: Calculate Simple Interest on Rs.4250 for 5 years at 8% p.a. rate of interest.
hints: Use SI = P × R × T ÷ 100. Try finding 1% of 4250 first.

questionText: Find the rate of interest if Rs.28500 amounts to Rs.38760 in three years.
hints: Amount = Principal + Interest. Find the interest first, then use R = SI × 100 ÷ (P × T).

questionText: What amount will you have to invest to earn SI of Rs.280 per month at 15% p.a. rate of interest?
hints: The rate is per YEAR but the interest is per MONTH. Convert Rs.280 a month into a yearly interest first.

questionText: Find SI if Rs.16000 is invested for 18 months at 8% p.a.
hints: Time must be in YEARS. How many years is 18 months?
18 months = 1.5 years. SI = P × R × T ÷ 100.

questionText: Rs.500 is invested at 12% simple interest. What is the amount after 5 years?
hints: The amount is the money at the start plus the interest it earns. 12% simple interest means every Rs.100 earns Rs.12 each year.
Find the interest for 1 year first: Rs.500 is 5 hundreds, and each hundred earns Rs.12. Multiply by 5 for the 5 years. Then add that interest to the Rs.500 you started with.
Try another one: Rs.200 at 4% for 3 years. Rs.200 is 2 hundreds, so 1 year earns 2 × 4 = 8 rupees. 3 years earn 3 × 8 = 24 rupees. Add the money at the start: 200 + 24 = 224. So the amount is Rs.224.

questionText: Rs.1500 is invested at 6% simple interest. What is the amount after 2 years?
hints: The amount is the money at the start plus the interest it earns. 6% simple interest means every Rs.100 earns Rs.6 each year.

Try another one: Rs.200 at 5% for 3 years. Rs.200 is 2 hundreds, so 1 year earns 2 × 5 = 10 rupees. 3 years earn 3 × 10 = 30 rupees. Add the money at the start: 200 + 30 = 230. So the amount is Rs.230.

questionText: Find the simple interest on Rs.1500 at 5% per annum for 5 years.
hints: Simple interest is the extra money that a sum of money earns. 5% per annum means every Rs.100 earns Rs.5 each year, and it earns the same again every year.
First find the interest for 1 year: Rs.1500 is 15 hundreds, and each hundred earns Rs.5. Then multiply that 1-year interest by 5 for the 5 years.
Try another one: Rs.200 at 4% for 3 years. Rs.200 is 2 hundreds, so 1 year earns 2 × 4 = 8 rupees. 3 years earn 3 × 8 = 24 rupees. So the simple interest is Rs.24.
